\chapter{Project roadmap}
\label{src:CCI_Project_Roadmap.md}
\Needspace{5\baselineskip}\section{Original CCI-Class Controller - Project Roadmap}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Target:} CEI 0-16 Annex O/T/M compliant Central Plant Controller, flexible 100 kW-6 MW MT plant range
  \item \textbf{Scope:} Original hardware/firmware design (not a clone of any existing commercial product)
  \item \textbf{Prototype budget:} \textasciitilde{}€1,000 (single unit, BOM + fab + assembly)
  \item \textbf{Timeline stance:} Balanced - solid working prototype in \textasciitilde{}10-12 weeks; grid/cyber certification is a separate, longer track
  \item \textbf{Existing certification:} organization already holds \textbf{ATEX} (EN/IEC 60079) - reuse QMS, Notified Body relationship, and technical-file practice for the CEI 0-16 track.
  \item \textbf{Alternate track:} see companion brief \textbf{CCLI-CLONE-RE-001} (\file{CCI\_Clone\_RE\_Option.pdf}) for the clone / reverse-engineering option, risks, and decision guide.
  \item [OK] \textbf{Already in place:} your company is \textbf{ATEX-certified}. Standard MT CCI cabinets are usually \emph{non-hazardous area} - confirm per project whether Ex marking is required on the CCI itself.
  \item [!] \textbf{Set expectations up front:} the hardware prototype is the \emph{cheap and fast} part. Remaining certification for this product (IEC 62443, IEC 61850, IEC 62351, CEI 0-16 demo) is realistically \textbf{€45,000-110,000+} and 9-18 months. ATEX is not budgeted again here.
\end{itemize}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{System architecture (original design)}
This block diagram reflects the \emph{generic, publicly-documented functional interfaces} that CEI 0-16 Annexes O/T require of any CCI (dual DSO/Operator Ethernet separation, plant-side ports, serial link to the energy analyzer, time sync, DI/DO for status/command) - not any specific vendor's schematic or component selection. See \file{CCI\_Architecture.png} (primary visual) and \file{CCI\_Architecture.mermaid} (editable companion).
\textbf{Core functional blocks:}

\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Block & Function & Notes / track \\
\midrule
Design approach & Option A (default): original SoM + carrier from public CEI 0-16 interfaces & Primary track - independent schematic, layout, firmware \\
Design approach & Option B: clone via reverse engineering (AiLux-class reference) & See \textbf{CCLI-CLONE-RE-001} (\file{CCI\_Clone\_RE\_Option.pdf}) - higher IP/legal risk; gated research spike only \\
Compute module (SoM) & Runs embedded Linux, IEC 61850 server, Modbus master, PF2 control logic & Option A: Toradex/Variscite/Compulab-class. See Sec.2 \\
Ethernet interfaces (>=4 port managed switch or SoM+switch IC) & Eth\_A -> DSO; Eth\_B -> Operator; 2x plant ports & DSO/plant isolation required - two isolated PHYs/VLANs minimum \\
RS-485/RS-232 serial (x2, isolated) & Modbus RTU master to energy analyzer; IEC 60870-5-101 optional & Opto-isolated; map registers from datasheet \\
GNSS module & Time sync for timestamped measurements/events & u-blox-class module + antenna \\
Cellular modem (LTE Cat-1/Cat-4) & Remote config/monitoring, backup comms & Optional on rev A if DSO link is wired \\
Digital I/O & DI: 10-120 Vdc status; DO: dry contact curtailment relay & Critical PF2 path - re-implement on Option B, do not copy reference network \\
Secure element + secure boot & Root of trust, key storage, signed firmware & Option A: your key hierarchy; Option B: never reuse reference keys/boot chain \\
Local console & USB service port for commissioning/diagnostics & Outside certified control path \\
Power input & 12-24 Vdc wide-range isolated DC-DC & Box CCI UPS/battery context \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compute module: SoM + custom carrier}
\textbf{Decision (from our discussion): off-the-shelf industrial SoM, original carrier board design.}
Candidate SoM families to evaluate (pick based on Linux BSP maturity, industrial temp range, and 10-year longevity commitment - you need this for a utility-facing product):
\begin{itemize}
  \item Toradex Verdin iMX8M Mini/Plus
  \item Variscite DART-MX8M-Mini / DART-MX8M-Plus
  \item Compulab CL-SOM-iMX8
  \item NXP i.MX8M Mini EVK-class reference designs
\end{itemize}
All of these ship a maintained Yocto BSP, handle DDR/power-sequencing/thermal internally, and let your carrier board stay a straightforward 2-4 layer design (Ethernet PHYs, RS-485 transceivers, GNSS/LTE module sockets, DI/DO conditioning, power).
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}

\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Firmware architecture \& language choice}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{OS/BSP:} Yocto-based embedded Linux (matches SoM vendor's supported BSP) - gives you package management, OTA update tooling, and a known-good foundation auditors are familiar with.
  \item \textbf{Core control/protocol path (IEC 61850 server, Modbus master, PF2 curtailment logic, GOOSE handling):} C/C++. This is the code that will eventually face conformance and security audits - auditors and test labs are far more comfortable reviewing statically-typed, analyzable C/C++ than dynamic scripting languages, and real-time GOOSE timing requirements favor it anyway.
  \item \textbf{Config/commissioning tooling, local web console, diagnostics:} Python or a lightweight web stack is fine here - this code is outside the certified control-path boundary, so language choice is a productivity call, not a compliance one. Keep the boundary between "certified path" and "tooling" architecturally clean from day one - it makes scoping the IEC 62443-4-2 assessment much cheaper later.
  \item \textbf{IEC 61850 stack:} start on \textbf{[libiec61850](https://github.com/mz-automation/libiec61850)} (MZ Automation) for prototype/demo - \textbf{GPLv3} open-source core (MMS, GOOSE, SV, R-Session); \textbf{commercial licenses sold separately} by MZ Automation for shipping a closed product. Treat OSS as \emph{free to prototype, pay to ship} - budget the commercial license from day one. Evaluate commercial stacks (SISCO, Triangle MicroWorks) before paid conformance testing - see Sec.7.
  \item \textbf{Security baseline to build in from day one} (cheap now, expensive to retrofit later): secure boot chain, signed firmware images, TLS/DTLS for IEC 62351, key storage in the secure element, basic RBAC on the local console, audit logging. IEC 62443-4-1 specifically audits \emph{how} you built and maintain the product (your SDLC), not just what features it has - so start documenting your development process now, not after the fact.
\end{itemize}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Timeline - Phase 1: Hardware + firmware prototype (\textasciitilde{}10-12 weeks, balanced pace)}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Weeks & Milestone \\
\midrule
1-2 & Architecture freeze, SoM selection finalized, schematic capture starts \\
2-4 & Schematic complete + design review, long-lead parts ordered (SoM, LTE/GNSS modules) \\
4-6 & PCB layout, DFM check, Gerbers to fab \\
6-8 & Fab + assembly turnaround \\
8-10 & Hardware bring-up: power, boot, verify each interface (Ethernet x4, RS-485 x2, GNSS, LTE, DI/DO) \\
10-12 & Firmware integration: libiec61850 server running, Modbus master polling a real analyzer, DO-driven curtailment stub, local console reachable \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

\textbf{Exit criteria for this phase:} a DIN-rail prototype that boots reliably, exposes an IEC 61850 MMS server over Eth\_A, polls a Modbus energy analyzer over RS-485, timestamps data via GNSS, and can toggle a DO relay from a simulated DSO command. This is a credible demo/investor/pilot-partner artifact - it is \emph{not} yet field-deployable at a real MT POC.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Phase 2: Certification path (separate track, 9-18 months)}
\textbf{Scope note:} ATEX (EN/IEC 60079) is \textbf{already held} - not a new line item. Table covers remaining CEI/grid/cyber work.
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}

\toprule
Workstream & What it involves & Rough cost & Duration \\
\midrule
\textbf{ATEX (EN/IEC 60079)} & \textbf{Already certified} - reuse NB/QMS/technical-file process & Sunk / reuse & - \\
IEC 62443-4-1 & Secure SDLC process audit (partial overlap with ATEX QMS) & €10,000-30,000 & 2-5 months \\
IEC 62443-4-2 & Device security lab test (SL1 min, target SL2) & €15,000-40,000 & 2-4 months \\
IEC 61850 conformance & MMS/GOOSE/reporting lab test & €10,000-25,000 & 1-3 months \\

\normalsize
\par\smallskip

\textbf{All-in for remaining CEI-class CCI certification: roughly €45,000-110,000 over 9-18 months} (ATEX excluded).
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Team/skills needed}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Embedded hardware engineer (schematic + layout, comfortable with SoM carrier design)
  \item Embedded Linux/firmware engineer (Yocto, C/C++, protocol stacks)
  \item Someone who can own the IEC 62443-4-1 process documentation - leverage existing ATEX technical-file and NB workflow
  \item Accredited test lab relationship early - your ATEX Notified Body may partner on 62443/61850 scoping
\end{itemize}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{To do}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Confirm SoM family choice (Toradex vs Variscite vs Compulab) based on your BSP/tooling comfort and long-term sourcing preference.
  \item I can draft the interface list and pin budget (connector-by-connector) as a starting schematic outline - original to your design, not copied from any existing product.
  \item Get a scoping quote from one IEC 62443/61850 test lab now, even before hardware exists - their capacity and requirements should shape your firmware architecture decisions, not the other way around.
\end{enumerate}
Happy to start on the schematic-level interface/pin-budget document next, or go deeper on any single phase above.

\part{Vendor selection \& prototype BOM}
\chapter{Vendor selection (C1-C10)}
\label{src:knowledge-base-08-engineering-CCI_Vendor_Selection.md}
\Needspace{5\baselineskip}\section{CCI Vendor Selection - Product Analysis \& Dev-Kit Matrix}
\textbf{Document ID:} CCLI-VENDOR-SEL-001
\textbf{Revision:} 1.1
\textbf{Date:} 2026-07-25
\textbf{RAG source\_id:} \file{ccli-vendor-selection}
\textbf{Purpose:} Analyze each SoM vendor’s \textbf{product} (SoM + eval kit + optional industrial gateway) against the CEI 0-16 / AiLux-class CCI control set, then choose a \textbf{development kit} for Phase 1 firmware - without treating the kit as the field product.
\textbf{Companions:} \file{CCI\_SoM\_Comparison} (silicon), \file{CCI\_Project\_Roadmap} (Option A), \file{CCI\_Module\_Regulations\_Classification} (protocol/cyber).
\textbf{Download index:} [\file{../DOWNLOADS.md}](../DOWNLOADS.md)
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Decision rule (read first)}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Layer & Role & Deploy as CCI? \\
\midrule
\textbf{SoM} & Production compute on \textbf{custom carrier} & Yes (with carrier) \\
\textbf{Dev / evaluation board} & BSP, Linux, early 61850/Modbus, signed-boot experiments & \textbf{No} \\
\textbf{Industrial gateway} (vendor SKU) & Reference for I/O patterns / BSP maturity & Usually \textbf{No} - form factor \& CEI Eth\_A/B story rarely match \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

\textbf{Phase 1 buy:} one vendor’s SoM + matching eval kit.
\textbf{Phase 1 build:} custom carrier for missing controls (extra Ethernet, isolated RS-485, field DI/DO, GNSS/LTE).
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Table A - CCI control checklist (master requirements)}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=0.900\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.300\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=0.900\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=0.900\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
ID & Requirement & Prototype kit & Product (carrier + SoM) \\
\midrule
C1 & >=4x 10/100 Ethernet: Eth\_A (DSO), Eth\_B (Operatore Abilitato / Qualified Operator), 2x plant & Partial OK (2 ports for SW demo) & \textbf{Required} \\
C2 & 2x opto-isolated RS-485 (Modbus RTU) on RJ45-class plant serial & 1x UART/RS232 OK for Modbus demo & \textbf{Required} \\
C3 & IEC 61850 Server/Client/GOOSE on Eth\_A & \textbf{Required} (SW on kit) & \textbf{Required} \\
C4 & DI 10-120 Vdc x5 (external field supply) / DO relay x3 & Stub in SW OK & \textbf{Required} \\
C5 & GNSS (GPS/GLONASS) time sync + SMA path & Nice-to-have & \textbf{Required} \\
C6 & Secure boot + key storage (HAB + SE/TPM path) & BSP proof on kit & \textbf{Required} \\
C7 & Maintained Yocto/Torizon BSP, industrial-temp SoM SKU & \textbf{Required} & \textbf{Required} \\
C8 & Longevity / PCN (\textasciitilde{}10-year industrial) & No & \textbf{Required} \\
C9 & Vendor signed-boot / security docs & Strongly preferred & \textbf{Required} \\
C10 & Power 12-24 Vdc class, DIN-rail product path & Eval may differ & \textbf{Required} \\
\bottomrule

\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Module inventory (source description)}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Inventario modulo (descrizione sorgente)}
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{1.0 Full source text (IT) + English translation}
\textbf{Italiano (originale):}
\begin{quote}
CPU iMX6D ARM Cortex-A9, 1GB DDR3, 4GByte eMMC, 800Mhz, CAAM, CSU, A-HAB SHA-256. Cyber Security: Secure Boot, Trusted Platform Module 2.0, FIPS 140-2 Level 3, RBAC, TRNG. Anti-Tamper hardware con switch collegato alla copertura e accelerometro X-Y-Z antimanomissione. Conforme a IEC-62443-4-1/2. Ethernet Switch a 4 porte 10/100 Mbps: una porta dedicata a DSO (ETH\_A) e una porta dedicata a Operatore Abilitato (ETH\_B); due porte per connessioni agli Elementi di Impianto; connettori RJ45 8/8. Due porte Seriali optoisolate RS-232/RS-485 su RJ45 8/8 standard ModBus. Una porta USB 2.0 per Consolle di Configurazione e Manutenzione Locale; due porte USB 2.0 per Elementi di Impianto. Protocolli seriali: IEC 61158-15 ModBus-RTU; IEC 60870-5-101 Balance/Unbalance; IEC 60870-5-103. Protocolli Ethernet: IEC 60870-5-104 Slave/Reverse/Redundancy (Gestione Armamenti Multicast/Unicast); IEC-61850 Server/Client/Goose; ModBus-TCP/IP Master/Slave; DNP3; S7-Comm; OPC-UA Client; C37.118 Client; IEC 62056-21 (DLMS/COSEM). Protocolli sicuri IEC 62351 parti 3-9 e 14. Servizi: http(s), sftp, ssh, snmp v2/v3 trap, ntpd, client/server PTP (IEEE-1588 power profile), redundancy cover system, firewall, RBAC, tasks ladder IEC 61131-3, web interface diagnostica/logs/SCADA. N°5 Ingressi Digitali optoisolati 10-120 Vdc (alimentazione esterna di campo); N°3 Uscite Digitali a relè 250 Vac 3A; GPS/GLONASS; modem 2G/3G/4G/LTE Cat.1; display OLED 1"; MicroSD fino a 32 GB; alimentazione 12-24 Vdc ±20\% 5 W; temperatura di esercizio -5 °C…+45 °C. Normative di riferimento: CEI 0-16 allegati O-T; CEI EN 61557-12:2018; ARERA 540/2021; FIPS 140-2; IEC 62351-3/-4/-5/-6.
\end{quote}
\textbf{English:}
\begin{quote}
CPU: i.MX6D ARM Cortex-A9, 1 GB DDR3, 4 GB eMMC, 800 MHz, CAAM, CSU, A-HAB SHA-256. Cybersecurity: Secure Boot, TPM 2.0, FIPS 140-2 Level 3, RBAC, TRNG. Hardware anti-tamper with cover-linked switch and X-Y-Z anti-tampering accelerometer. Compliant with IEC 62443-4-1/2. 4-port 10/100 Mbps Ethernet switch: one port dedicated to the DSO (ETH\_A), one port dedicated to the Qualified/Authorized Operator (ETH\_B); two ports for connections to plant elements (DER field devices); RJ45 8/8 connectors. Two opto-isolated serial ports RS-232/RS-485 on RJ45 8/8 Modbus pinout. One USB 2.0 port for local configuration \& maintenance console; two USB 2.0 ports for plant elements. Serial protocols: IEC 61158-15 Modbus-RTU; IEC 60870-5-101 balanced/unbalanced; IEC 60870-5-103. Ethernet protocols: IEC 60870-5-104 Slave/Reverse/Redundancy (arming management via multicast and unicast); IEC 61850 Server/Client/GOOSE; Modbus-TCP/IP Master/Slave; DNP3; S7-Comm; OPC-UA Client; C37.118 Client; IEC 62056-21 (DLMS/COSEM). Secure protocols: IEC 62351 parts 3-9 and 14. Services: http(s), sftp, ssh, SNMP v2/v3 trap, ntpd, PTP client/server (IEEE 1588 power profile), redundancy cover system, firewall, RBAC, IEC 61131-3 ladder tasks, web UI for diagnostics/logs/SCADA. 5 opto-isolated digital inputs 10-120 Vdc (external field supply); 3 relay digital outputs 250 Vac / 3 A; GPS/GLONASS; 2G/3G/4G/LTE Cat.1 modem; 1" OLED; MicroSD up to 32 GB; supply 12-24 Vdc ±20\%, 5 W; operating temperature -5 °C…+45 °C. Reference standards: CEI 0-16 Annexes O-T; CEI EN 61557-12:2018; ARERA Decision 540/2021; FIPS 140-2; IEC 62351-3/-4/-5/-6.
\end{quote}

\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Notes / caveats / Note}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{IEC 61158-15} is the fieldbus family reference often used commercially for Modbus; confirm exact Modbus.org / IEC edition when purchasing standards.
  \item \textbf{S7-Comm} is proprietary - no public IEC PDF expected; keep as protocol capability only.
  \item \textbf{FIPS 140-2 Level 3} is a \emph{crypto module} claim (typically TPM); do not treat as whole-device FIPS certification unless a certificate number is provided.
  \item \textbf{IEC 62443-4-1/2 “conforme” / “compliant with”} on a competitor datasheet is a claim - clone path needs evidence (SDL artifacts + component requirements) before CE/CRA arguments.
  \item This classification document is \textbf{not} a substitute for licensed standard PDFs; it routes RAG until those PDFs are ingested. / Questo documento \textbf{non} sostituisce i PDF delle norme: serve al routing RAG finché non sono ingeriti.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{Industrial RAG architecture}
\label{src:knowledge-base-08-engineering-CCI_Industrial_RAG_Architecture.md}
\Needspace{5\baselineskip}\section{CCI Industrial RAG Architecture (three indexes)}
\textbf{Doc ID:} CCLI-RAG-ARCH-001
\textbf{Revision:} 1.0
\textbf{Date:} 2026-07-25
\textbf{Target score:} \textasciitilde{}9.8/10 industrial engineering RAG (from \textasciitilde{}8.5/10 vector-first baseline)
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Three indexes}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Index & Role & Where \\
\midrule
\textbf{Vector} & Semantic similarity over chunk embeddings & Telematry SQLite \file{chunks.embedding\_json} (+ optional Qdrant) \\
\textbf{Keyword} & Exact token / acronym retrieval (HAB, TPM, IEC62351, 99991105…) & Token overlap + exact-term boost; optional Elasticsearch BM25 \\
\textbf{Knowledge graph} & Typed reasoning paths & Seed JSON + SQLite \file{graph\_edges} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

\textbf{Hybrid fusion (query time):}
\begin{verbatim}
score = 0.50 x vector + 0.50 x keyword
      + chunk_type_boost + context_boost + entity_overlap_boost
      + exact_industrial_term_boost (capped)
\end{verbatim}
Then attach \textbf{seed graph paths} and \textbf{missing\_sources} (from regulatory map) into query traces / citation \file{graph\_paths}.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}

\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}

\toprule
Artifact & Path \\
\midrule

\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Edge types (seed graph)}
\file{ENABLES} · \file{IMPLEMENTS} · \file{REQUIRES} · \file{MAPS\_TO} · \file{COVERED\_BY} · \file{\statuspartial{}} · \file{\statusmissing{}} · \file{CERT\_CLAIM} · \file{RELATED}
Example spine:
\begin{verbatim}
i.MX 8 -> TrustZone -> Secure Boot -> HAB
Eth_A -> IEC 61850 -> IEC 62351
Verdin 99991105 -[PARTIAL]-> C1 Ethernet
Verdin 99991105 -[MISSING]-> C2 RS-485 / C4 DI/DO / C5 GNSS
\end{verbatim}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Query contract (already on \file{/v1/query})}
Request: \file{tenant\_id}, \file{bot\_id}, \file{query}, \file{source\_ids[]}, \file{top\_k}, \file{grounding\_prompt}.
Response traces now include:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \file{hybrid\_mode}
  \item \file{query\_entities}
  \item \file{seed\_graph\_paths}
  \item \file{missing\_sources} (\statusmissing{}/\statuspartial{} norms from seed \file{rag\_status\_refs})
  \item Citations carry \file{graph\_paths} + \file{chunk\_metadata.entity\_names} (after re-ingest)
\end{itemize}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Apply after code deploy}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Restart RAG container / process so new dictionaries and scoring load.
  \item Re-ingest CCLI sources so chunk metadata gets CCI entities:
\end{enumerate}
\begin{verbatim}
cd "C:\Yahia\projects\Telematry System"
.\scripts\ingest-ccli.ps1
\end{verbatim}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Smoke-test:
\end{enumerate}
\begin{verbatim}
$body = @{
  tenant_id = "telematry"; bot_id = "default"
  query = "What CCI controls does Toradex Verdin 99991105 not cover regarding HAB and RS-485?"
  source_ids = @("ccli-vendor-selection","ccli-toradex-verdin-devboard","ccli-cci-module-regs-class")
  top_k = 8; answer_language = "en"; clarify = $false
} | ConvertTo-Json
Invoke-RestMethod http://localhost:8001/v1/query -Method POST -Body $body -ContentType "application/json" |
  Select-Object -ExpandProperty traces | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
\end{verbatim}
Expect: \file{query\_entities} containing \file{hab} / \file{verdin} / \file{rs485}, \file{seed\_graph\_paths} with \statuspartial{}/\statusmissing{} edges, \file{missing\_sources} empty or limited unless norms are asked.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}

  \item Full Okapi BM25 / SQLite FTS5 inverted index (today: overlap + exact boost + optional ES)
  \item Semantic re-chunking pass (heading/table-aware) beyond current classifiers
  \item LLM entity extraction second pass

\part{Validation \& test}
\chapter{PF2 validation \& mocking strategy}
\label{src:knowledge-base-08-engineering-CCI_Validation_and_Mocking_Strategy.md}
\Needspace{5\baselineskip}\section{CCI Validation \& Mocking Strategy - PF2 Bench Ladder}
\textbf{Document ID:} CCLI-VAL-001
\textbf{Revision:} 1.0
\textbf{Date:} 2026-07-25
\textbf{RAG source\_id:} \file{ccli-validation-strategy}
\textbf{Purpose:} Define a progressive, evidence-based bench strategy for validating Modbus metering, PF2 logic, IEC 61850/104, digital I/O, logging, and safe fault handling before plant deployment.
\textbf{Companions:} \file{CCI\_Mocking\_Bench\_BOM.md} | \file{CCI\_Prototype\_BOM.md} | \file{CCI\_Vendor\_Selection.md} | \file{CCI\_Project\_Roadmap.md}
\begin{quote}
This ladder validates engineering behavior; it does \textbf{not} replace accredited CEI 0-16 demonstrations, IEC 61850 conformance testing, EMC/safety testing, or IEC 62443 product/process assessment.
\end{quote}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Recommended progression}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=0.900\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.300\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=0.900\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=0.900\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Level & Bench & Main value & Phase 1 gate \\
\midrule
\textbf{L1 - Software mock} & PC-hosted Modbus/IEC protocol simulators & Fast, deterministic application tests & \textbf{Required first} \\
\textbf{L2 - Interface HIL} & Controller + physical Ethernet/RS-485 + emulator PC & Drivers, timing, framing, cable faults & \textbf{Recommended Phase 1} \\
\textbf{L3 - Real analyzer} & Controller + selected energy analyzer & Vendor register map and device behavior & \textbf{Required before field pilot} \\
\textbf{L4 - Power-system HIL} & Typhoon HIL / OPAL-RT / RTDS-class real-time simulator & Closed-loop grid/inverter/protection behavior & Later system-validation campaign \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

Do not jump directly to L3 or L4. Keep the same versioned test vectors and expected outcomes across all levels so failures can be isolated to software, interface, device integration, or closed-loop behavior.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Level 1 - software-only mocking}
Run a Modbus server on an engineering PC. The controller polls it using the same application code, register map abstraction, scaling, timeout policy, and PF2 state machine intended for the product.
\begin{verbatim}
Engineering PC
+-- Modbus TCP/RTU simulator
    +-- P = 850 kW
    +-- Q = 100 kvar
    +-- power factor = 0.98
\end{verbatim}
Candidate tools: \textbf{pymodbus simulator}, \textbf{ModbusPal}, \textbf{QModMaster}, and \textbf{ModRSsim2}. Tool selection is not frozen; record the exact version and configuration in each test report.
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{2.1 Minimum scenarios}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Test ID & Stimulus & Expected controller behavior \\
\midrule
L1-P-01 & P = 500 kW & No curtailment \\
L1-P-02 & P = 700 kW & No curtailment \\
L1-P-03 & P = 950 kW & Curtailment request after configured debounce \\
L1-P-04 & P = 1,000 kW & Curtailment remains active; no repeated command storm \\
L1-C-01 & Meter timeout & Quality invalid, alarm/event, configured safe state \\
L1-C-02 & Illegal function / exception response & Diagnostic event; no stale value treated as valid \\
L1-C-03 & Bad CRC (RTU) & Frame rejected and counted; retry policy applied \\
L1-D-01 & Out-of-range / NaN-equivalent register pattern & Input rejected or clamped per ICD; alarm raised \\
L1-R-01 & Process restart & State recovery follows persistence and fail-safe policy \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

\textbf{Important:} bad-CRC and malformed-frame injection may require a purpose-built serial fault proxy or test script; many general Modbus simulators only emit valid frames.
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{2.2 PF2 reference sequence}
Illustrative rule only: \textbf{if valid active power P > 900 kW, request curtailment}.
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Time & P & Expected \\
\midrule
00:00 & 500 kW & No action \\
00:30 & 700 kW & No action \\
01:00 & 950 kW & Curtail after debounce \\
01:30 & 1,000 kW & Curtail remains active \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

The production test must also define hysteresis, debounce, minimum on/off time, stale-data timeout, command acknowledgement, manual override, restart behavior, and release threshold. A single \file{P > 900} comparison is not sufficient for a safe controller.
Verify every transition through:
\begin{itemize}
  \item PF2 state-machine state and reason code
  \item digital-output intent (mocked at L1)
  \item IEC 61850 / IEC 104 / Modbus command intent, where applicable
  \item alarm generation and acknowledgement
  \item timestamped event and measurement logs
  \item input quality, source, engineering units, and scaling
\end{itemize}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Level 2 - physical-interface HIL (recommended)}
Use the real controller serial and Ethernet interfaces while the plant-side device remains emulated.
\begin{verbatim}
CCI controller
    |
    +-- RS-485 cable -- USB-to-RS-485 adapter -- Linux PC emulator
    +-- Ethernet ----- engineering switch ----- protocol test client
\end{verbatim}
This validates:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Linux UART/serial driver and device-tree mapping
  \item RS-485 direction control, polarity, termination, and bias
  \item configured baud rate, parity, stop bits, slave address, retries, and timeout
  \item real frame timing and recovery after disconnect/reconnect
  \item Ethernet interface binding and Eth\_A/Eth\_B policy
  \item controller CPU/load behavior under protocol traffic
\end{itemize}
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{3.1 C2 limitation on lead eval hardware}
The Toradex Verdin Development Board \textbf{99991105} provides \textbf{one non-isolated RS-485 DB9 path}. It is suitable for early L2 software/driver testing, but it does not prove the product requirement of \textbf{two opto-isolated RS-485 RJ45-class plant ports}. Repeat the electrical tests on the custom carrier.
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{3.2 L2 fault injection}
\begin{itemize}
  \item unplug/reconnect RS-485 while polling
  \item reverse A/B during a controlled test
  \item remove termination or introduce a long/noisy cable
  \item use wrong baud/parity/slave ID
  \item delay responses beyond timeout
  \item disconnect Eth\_A, Eth\_B, and plant Ethernet independently
  \item restart the emulator while the controller remains online
\end{itemize}
For each case verify bounded retries, no task deadlock, invalid data quality, event logging, alarm lifecycle, and a defined safe state.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Level 3 - real energy analyzer}
Connect the selected production-candidate analyzer, for example a Schneider PM, Janitza UMG, Carlo Gavazzi, or Siemens PAC family device. The exact model and firmware must be frozen in the test record.
A real analyzer validates:
\begin{itemize}
  \item vendor register addresses, word order, signedness, scaling, and units
  \item update rate and communication latency
  \item device exception behavior and configuration persistence
  \item voltage, current, active/reactive/apparent power, frequency, power factor, and quality flags
\end{itemize}
No high-power plant is required for communications testing. Use the analyzer's supported test/simulation mode, low-voltage injection equipment, or a calibrated secondary-injection source as appropriate.
\textbf{Do not assume arbitrary register values can be manually configured on every analyzer.} Confirm the chosen model's test mode and obtain its official \textbf{Modbus register map}; this remains a P1 missing document in the prototype BOM.
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{4.1 L3 acceptance gate}
\begin{itemize}
  \item official register map is on disk and ingested
  \item every consumed register has address, type, scale, unit, validity rule, and polling rate
  \item controller readings agree with analyzer display/reference within declared tolerance
  \item loss/recovery and analyzer reboot tests pass
  \item firmware/model-specific deviations are documented
\end{itemize}
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Level 4 - real-time power-system HIL}
Use a Typhoon HIL, OPAL-RT, RTDS, or equivalent real-time platform when closed-loop interaction with a modeled grid, inverter, transformer, protection relay, and communications network is justified.
The controller may receive and emit:
\begin{itemize}
  \item IEC 61850 MMS, reports, and GOOSE
  \item IEC 60870-5-104
  \item Modbus RTU/TCP
  \item DI/DO and analog/measurement signals through suitable I/O interfaces
\end{itemize}
Use L4 to test dynamic ramps, oscillation, command delays, protection events, communications congestion, failover, and interactions among PF2 logic, inverter controls, and DSO/operator commands.
L4 is valuable but expensive. It is \textbf{not required to start Phase 1}, and it does not itself certify CEI 0-16 or IEC 61850 conformance.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Digital-input test box (C4)}
Product target: \textbf{5 opto-isolated DI channels, 10-120 Vdc, external field supply}.
Use a guarded, fused test fixture with selectable supported voltages (typically 24 V, 48 V, and 110 V where the final input design permits). Inject named states such as breaker closed/open, alarm active, meter fault, and external permissive.
Verify:
\begin{itemize}
  \item asserted/deasserted thresholds and hysteresis
  \item polarity protection and channel isolation
  \item debounce and contact chatter behavior
  \item Linux GPIO/application state mapping
  \item event timestamp and source identity
  \item simultaneous-channel transitions
  \item open-wire/power-loss behavior where detectable
\end{itemize}
\textbf{Safety:} 110 Vdc is hazardous. Use current limiting, fusing, guarded terminals, an emergency disconnect, and competent personnel. Start at 24 V until the carrier input circuit has passed design review.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Dry-contact output tests (C4)}
Connect each relay output to a safe indicator lamp, PLC input, or isolated digital-input module. Do not switch mains loads during early bench testing.
\begin{verbatim}
PF2 active -> output policy permits actuation -> relay closes -> lamp/PLC input ON
\end{verbatim}
Measure:
\begin{itemize}
  \item command-to-contact response time
  \item contact bounce and application filtering
  \item power-up, reboot, watchdog, and power-loss state
  \item normally-open/normally-closed interpretation
  \item stuck relay / feedback mismatch handling if feedback is available
  \item manual override and command interlock behavior
\end{itemize}
The safe state must be specified by the system safety/control analysis; "relay open" is not automatically safe for every plant.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{IEC 61850 and IEC 104 bench}
\begin{verbatim}
IED test client / protocol emulator
              |
          Ethernet switch
              |
         CCI controller
\end{verbatim}
Test MMS reads, control writes with the configured control model, buffered/unbuffered reports, GOOSE publish/subscribe, dataset/configuration revision handling, time quality, disconnect/reconnect, and malformed or unauthorized requests.
Candidate tools include \textbf{Omicron IEDScout}, \textbf{Omicron StationScout}, and test clients built from \textbf{libiec61850}. libiec61850 is suitable for prototyping under GPLv3; a commercial license is required for a closed shipped product.
For IEC 60870-5-104, test connection supervision, sequence counters, time-tagged events, command select/execute if used, spontaneous transmissions, and reconnect behavior.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Cross-interface failure matrix}
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Failure & Required checks \\
\midrule
Meter disconnected / RS-485 cut & Invalid quality, alarm, event, bounded retry, safe PF2 behavior \\
Eth\_A disconnected & DSO link alarm; plant functions remain bounded \\
Eth\_B disconnected & Operator link alarm; no unauthorized fallback \\
GNSS lost & Time-quality downgrade; holdover policy; event \\
LTE lost & Backup-link alarm; primary control path unaffected \\
Process crash / watchdog reset & Controlled restart; outputs go to defined state \\
Stale measurement & Never treated as current; command inhibition or fallback per policy \\
Conflicting DSO/operator/local command & Deterministic priority and audit trail \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

The most important acceptance criterion is not "an alarm appeared"; it is that a communication fault cannot cause uncontrolled curtailment or silent use of stale data.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Practical Phase 1 PF2 bench}
\begin{verbatim}
Engineering PC
+-- IEC 61850 / IEC 104 client and traffic capture
+-- Modbus simulator and test-vector runner
+-- USB-to-RS-485 adapter
             |
        Ethernet switch
             |
       CCI controller / Verdin kit
        +-- DI test box (24 V first)
        +-- DO test lamps / isolated PLC inputs
\end{verbatim}
This bench can validate most application behavior without a solar plant, inverter, or grid connection:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Modbus RTU/TCP acquisition
  \item PF2 state machine and command arbitration
  \item IEC 61850 and IEC 104 application behavior
  \item DI/DO mapping on suitable hardware
  \item logging, alarms, time quality, and fault handling
  \item basic cybersecurity controls and interface separation
\end{itemize}
It cannot prove final carrier isolation/EMC, analyzer accuracy, full power-system dynamics, or product conformance.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}
\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Test evidence required}
Every test case should record:
\par\smallskip\noindent
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X>{\hsize=1.000\hsize\RaggedRight\arraybackslash}X}
\toprule
Field & Required content \\
\midrule
Test ID / revision & Stable identifier linked to requirement C1-C10 \\
Build identity & Git commit, image/BSP version, configuration hash \\
Equipment & Model, serial number, firmware, calibration status where relevant \\
Topology & Ports, cables, addresses, baud/parity, VLAN/interface binding \\
Stimulus & Exact values and fault timing \\
Expected result & State, output, alarm, log, timing limit \\
Actual result & Captures, logs, contact measurement, screenshots \\
Verdict & PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED with defect reference \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\normalsize
\par\smallskip

Prefer machine-readable test vectors (JSON/YAML/CSV) plus an automated runner for L1/L2. Preserve packet captures, serial traces, and controller logs as evidence artifacts.
\par\vspace{0.35em}\noindent\textcolor{HiteksOrange}{\rule{\linewidth}{0.4pt}}\par\vspace{0.35em}

  \item Pick MPNs + DS for \textbf{D11-D14} (C4, C1, C2, C10)
  \item Author PF2 spec + Modbus test vectors (\file{ccli-app-pf2})
\end{enumerate}
\Needspace{3\baselineskip}\subsubsection{P2 - product / optional}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Licensed norm PDFs (ARERA, 61557-12, 62443, 62351)
  \item \textbf{D7} ActiveBOM after Altium
  \item \textbf{D18} enclosure drawing
\end{enumerate}

\Needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Quick lookup - lead path minimum pin set}
Order of operations when Toradex kit \textbf{99991105} + SoM \textbf{0063} arrives:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \file{git.toradex.com/toradex-manifest.git} - record \textbf{default.xml} revision
  \item All layers referenced by that manifest - record \textbf{SHA per project}
  \item \file{github.com/toradex/meta-toradex-security} @ matching branch - record SHA
  \item \file{github.com/toradex/build-signed-imx8m-bootloader} @ \file{scarthgap-7.x.y} - record SHA
  \item \file{github.com/nxp-imx/meta-imx} - only if pulled by manifest (verify)
  \item \file{github.com/Freescale/meta-freescale} @ \file{scarthgap} - record SHA
  \item Application pins: \file{libiec61850}, \file{lib60870} - record \textbf{release tag} for recipes
\end{enumerate}
